meta.title: RAG Evaluation and Faithfulness
meta.thesis: RAG Evaluation and Faithfulness is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A RAG answer sounds fluent but may include claims not supported by retrieved chunks. By the end, they should be able to build or review faithfulness evaluation rubric with claim-level support checks, measure unsupported claim rate per answer, and catch the failure where the answer is relevant to the question but adds facts outside the evidence.

mentalMap.title: RAG Evaluation and Faithfulness: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Evaluate retrieval, context support, and final answer faithfulness as separate signals.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: RAG faithfulness means the answer’s claims are supported by the retrieved context; it is not the same as fluency or topical relevance.

modules.title: Faithfulness is support, not confidence
modules.sub: An answer is faithful only if context proves it.
modules.summary: A fluent answer with weak citations is still a RAG failure.

blocks.title: Citations are not automatically evidence

spans.text: Problem anchor: a RAG assistant answers “Enterprise refunds require finance approval,” cites the refund page, but the retrieved chunk only covers standard plans. The citation is real, but it does not support the claim.
Faithfulness asks whether the answer can be derived from the provided context. It is stricter than “the answer sounds right” and different from “the retrieved chunk is on the same topic.”
Highlight every factual claim in the answer, then point to the exact retrieved sentence or table cell that supports it.

blocks.analogy: A citation is a receipt only if it lists the item you claim to bought.

spans.text: Answer sentence: “Enterprise refunds after 30 days need finance approval.” Retrieved context A says “standard refunds within 30 days.” Context B says “enterprise exceptions require finance approval after 30 days.”
Only context B supports the sentence. If context B is absent, the faithful answer should say the evidence is insufficient or restrict itself to standard refunds.

items.text: Break the answer into factual claims.
Map each claim to a retrieved source span.
Mark unsupported, contradicted, or overgeneralized claims.
Feed failures back to retrieval, prompting, or refusal logic.

blocks.title: Faithfulness check
blocks.prompt: A citation is on-topic but lacks the fact stated in the answer. How should it be judged?

options.text: Faithful because the URL exists.
Unfaithful or unsupported for that claim.
Correct because the model sounded confident.

blocks.explanation: Faithfulness depends on support in retrieved context.

modules.title: Evaluate retrieval before generation
modules.sub: The answer cannot be faithful to missing evidence.
objectives: Use hit rate, recall at k, MRR, and context precision.
Measure packed top-k, not only candidate top-k.

blocks.title: Retrieval is the evidence supply chain

spans.text: A generated answer can fail because the retriever missed the document, ranked it too low, packed noisy context above it, or supplied stale evidence. These are retrieval failures even if the model behaves normally.
Source-based eval cases are powerful: for each query, record which source or fact should appear. Then measure whether it appears inside the actual context window used for generation.
If the correct source appears at rank 18 but the prompt packs 6 chunks, count that as a failure for the shipped app.

blocks.analogy: Do not grade the chef before checking whether the ingredients arrived.

blocks.title: Case study: top-20 success, top-6 failure

spans.text: A retrieval report shows 92% hit@20, but answers remain wrong. The prompt only packs top 6, and expected sources appear between rank 9 and 15 for policy exception questions.
The fix is reranking or chunking, not a friendlier answer prompt. The metric changes to packed-context hit rate.

items.text: Record expected source IDs for each query.
Run the production retriever and prompt packer.
Measure source presence within packed top-k.
Bucket misses by chunking, filters, stale index, or ranking.

blocks.title: Retrieval metric

options.text: Hit@20 only works for images.
The generator may only receive the top few chunks, so rank 20 evidence is invisible.
The model automatically reads the whole database.

blocks.explanation: Measure the context the model actually sees.

modules.title: Use judges carefully and keep raw evidence
modules.sub: LLM metrics help, but traces keep them honest.
modules.summary: Automated evaluation is useful when paired with examples and thresholds.
objectives: Name context precision, recall, response relevancy, and faithfulness.

blocks.title: Metrics are diagnostics, not verdicts from the sky

spans.text: Tools such as Ragas provide metrics for context quality, response relevancy, and faithfulness. These metrics are useful for regression checks, especially when paired with a stable evaluation set.
However, LLM-as-judge scores can vary and may miss policy-sensitive nuance. Keep raw question, retrieved context, answer, references, and judge rationale so humans can inspect high-impact failures.
Track aggregate scores by category; overall improvement can hide regressions in exact-identifier or compliance queries.

blocks.analogy: A judge score is a dashboard light; you still need to open the hood for serious failures.

cells.text: Expected source appears in packed top-k.
Does not prove the answer used it correctly.
Judge inconsistency and subtle policy nuance.

options.name: Manual review
options.whenToUse: Use for release samples and failures.

blocks.title: Judge caution
blocks.prompt: What should you keep when using LLM-based faithfulness scoring?

options.text: Only the final average score.
The raw question, retrieved context, answer, references, and rationale for review.
Only model latency.

blocks.explanation: Reviewable traces make automated metrics trustworthy.

modules.title: Implement a small retrieval eval loop
modules.sub: A few cases can catch major regressions.
objectives: Predict which test fails from retrieved IDs.

blocks.title: The first eval can be simple

spans.text: Before adding complex judges, write a loop that runs production retrieval for known questions and checks expected source IDs. This catches many chunking, filtering, and ranking regressions.
Spaced recall: from reranking, compare original and reranked ranks. Evaluation should reveal whether the reranker moved expected evidence into the packed context.
Include negative cases where no source should answer the question.

blocks.title: Source-based retrieval eval
blocks.explanation: This checks whether expected evidence appears and how early it appears, before any model answer is judged.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Before running it, predict which query has the lower reciprocal rank.
predictThenReveal.answer: The API-token query has MRR 0.5 because the expected source is second; the refund query also has 0.5 in this toy data.

blocks.title: Eval harness
blocks.prompt: What does reciprocal rank capture that hit@k does not?

options.text: Whether the answer uses rhyming language.
How early the first expected source appears.
The number of GPUs in the database.

blocks.explanation: Earlier evidence is more likely to fit into prompt context.

modules.title: Close the loop with regression thresholds
modules.sub: Evaluation matters only if it changes release decisions.
modules.summary: Faithfulness evaluation should block unsafe retrieval and generation changes.
objectives: Set thresholds for retrieval and faithfulness.
Use evals after document and model changes.

blocks.title: A RAG eval is a release contract

spans.text: Set thresholds that reflect product risk: packed-context hit rate, faithfulness pass rate, unsupported-claim count, negative-case behavior, and category-specific regressions. Do not rely only on a single average.

Run the suite after source updates, chunking changes, embedding migrations, reranker changes, prompt edits, and framework upgrades. A small, stable suite is better than an impressive report nobody reruns.
Every failed eval should point to a fix owner: ingestion, retrieval, generation, validation, or source content.

blocks.title: Verify AI output with faithfulness evaluation

spans.text: Before release, sample answers against these checks.

items.text: Each factual claim maps to a retrieved source span.
Expected sources appear inside the packed context, not only deep in candidates.
Negative cases refuse or qualify instead of inventing facts.
Judge scores are spot-checked with raw traces.
Failures are bucketed with an owner and rerun after fixes.

blocks.title: Release gate
blocks.prompt: A prompt edit improves response tone but increases unsupported claims. What should happen?

options.text: Ship because tone improved.
Block or revise the prompt because faithfulness regressed.
Delete the eval suite.

blocks.explanation: Groundedness is a core RAG requirement, not a nice-to-have metric.

rag.label: RAG
rag.laymanDefinition: Retrieving relevant evidence before generation so answers can be grounded in sources.
rag.technicalNote: RAG quality depends on corpus freshness, chunking, embeddings, filters, ranking, citation handling, and faithfulness evaluation.

embedding.label: Embedding
embedding.laymanDefinition: A numeric vector representation of text used for semantic comparison.
embedding.technicalNote: Embedding choices fix dimension, distance metric, query/passage formatting, model version, and migration requirements for retrieval.

vector_search.label: Vector search
vector_search.laymanDefinition: Finding nearby vectors to retrieve semantically related chunks.
vector_search.technicalNote: Vector search needs metadata filters, recall tests, index tuning, and fallback for exact terms, IDs, and rare phrases.

chunk.label: Chunk
chunk.laymanDefinition: A source text segment stored and retrieved as a unit.
chunk.technicalNote: Chunk design balances semantic completeness, citation accuracy, token budget, overlap, metadata, and update/delete behavior.

reranker.label: Reranker
reranker.laymanDefinition: A second-stage model or method that reorders retrieved candidates by relevance.
reranker.technicalNote: Rerankers improve top-result precision when candidate recall is adequate, but add latency, cost, and evaluation complexity.

rrf.label: RRF
rrf.laymanDefinition: A rank-fusion method that merges multiple result lists by reciprocal rank.
rrf.technicalNote: RRF is useful for hybrid retrieval because it combines lexical and vector rankings without requiring comparable raw scores.

finalCheck.title: Knowledge check
finalCheck.intro: A quick check across the whole lesson — pick or type your answers.

questions.prompt: A RAG system returns an answer that sounds highly confident and matches what a user expects — but none of the retrieved chunks actually state that fact. Is this answer faithful?

options.text: Yes, because the answer is relevant to the user's question.
No, because faithfulness requires the answer to be supported by the retrieved context, not just plausible.
Yes, because the model's confidence indicates it learned this from training data.
No, but only if the user explicitly flags it as wrong.

questions.explanation: Faithfulness is about grounding in the retrieved context — a confident or relevant-sounding answer that isn't backed by the retrieved chunks is still unfaithful.

questions.prompt: You run retrieval for 50 test queries. For 35 of them, the correct source document appears somewhere in the top-5 results. What is the Hit Rate @ 5?

options.text: It cannot be computed without knowing the rank of each correct document.

questions.explanation: Hit Rate @ k (hit@k) is simply the fraction of queries where the correct document appears anywhere in the top-k results: 35 ÷ 50 = 0.70, or 70%.

questions.prompt: Context Precision and Context Recall measure different things. Which statement correctly distinguishes them?

options.text: Context Precision measures how many relevant chunks were retrieved; Context Recall measures how short the context window is.
Context Precision measures what fraction of retrieved chunks are actually relevant; Context Recall measures what fraction of all relevant chunks were retrieved.
Context Precision and Context Recall are two names for the same metric, just reported differently.
Context Recall measures how faithfully the model used the retrieved chunks; Context Precision measures answer length.

questions.explanation: Precision asks 'of what I retrieved, how much was useful?' while Recall asks 'of everything useful that existed, how much did I retrieve?' — they capture opposite failure modes.

questions.prompt: You use an LLM-as-judge to score faithfulness across 200 responses. A colleague notices that rephrasing the same response slightly changes the judge's score. What is this problem called, and name one practical safeguard against it?
questions.acceptableAnswer: This is judge inconsistency (or judge variance / sensitivity). Practical safeguards include: keeping raw traces for manual review, running multiple judge passes and averaging, using a fixed scoring rubric/prompt, or spot-checking a sample of scores by hand.
questions.explanation: LLM judges can be sensitive to surface-level wording changes, so retaining raw evidence and spot-checking manually are essential safeguards against acting on unreliable scores.

questions.prompt: Your team ships a document update that adds 500 new product pages. According to a regression-threshold approach, what should happen next?

options.text: Wait for user complaints before re-running evals, to avoid wasting compute.
Re-run the retrieval and faithfulness eval suite and compare results against your established thresholds to catch regressions.
Only re-run faithfulness evals, because document changes cannot affect retrieval metrics.
Raise all thresholds by 10% to account for the larger document set.

questions.explanation: Document changes can shift both retrieval quality and faithfulness, so the eval loop should be triggered after any document or model change and results compared against fixed thresholds to detect regressions early.
